transport: Dry contact, no bus, no framing, no addressing. On a BatteryProtect: a switch between terminal Remote H and terminal Remote L; alternatively H switched high to battery positive, or L switched low to battery negative. Default state from the factory is a wire loop between L and H. On the ASS030550320 cable: signal high enables, signal <1 V or free floating disables; switch-on threshold approximately

gotchas: **Open and close are not symmetric in time.** The Smart BatteryProtect manual §4.4: the load is connected 1 second after the remote input closes, and disconnected *immediately* when the remote input opens. A rules engine that toggles on a 1 Hz tick can command a state the device has not reached yet.

**Li-ion mode adds a 30-second dead period.** In Li-ion mode the SBP observes a dead period of 30 seconds after the remote input becomes free floating. A retry loop that re-asserts the relay inside that window sees nothing happen and may escalate.

**Three consecutive disengage/re-engage cycles latch the unit off.** Error E7 (BMS lockout) fires when the remote input is cycled three times consecutively — the manual describes this as typical BMS behaviour during a low-cell-voltage shutdown. Once E7 is latched the SBP stays disengaged until input voltage exceeds 13

**The factory wire loop must come out.** The manual: "The wire loop in the remote on/off terminal block must be removed" before the remote input can be used. A gateway relay wired in parallel with an intact loop does nothing.

**Never wire an inverter's DC input through a BatteryProtect.** The manual is unambiguous: "Under no circumstances is it permitted to connect inverters or inverter/chargers to a SBP via their DC inputs, a reverse current may flow that damages the SBP." unmappedReports: Nothing is reported over this interface at all — it is an input to the device, not an output. `switch-state` can only be published as the state the gateway *commanded*, never as a state read back from the device. That is a real distinction the contract cannot express: there is no way to say "this value is open-loop". Any switch-state a driver publishes here is an assertion about its own relay, not an observation of the BatteryProtect., The alarm output is the one thing that flows the other way: an open-collector output to the negative rail, max 50 mA, short-circuit proof, present on both Smart and non-Smart BatteryProtect, asserted when the battery voltage stays below the disconnect level for more than 12 seconds. A gateway GPIO input could sense it. It is a *warning*, not a switch position, and the contract has no metric for it — `switch-state` would be a lie about what it means.
